What is MCP?

MCP is an open protocol that enables AI models to securely interact with local and remote resources through standardized server implementations. This list focuses on production-ready and experimental MCP servers that extend AI capabilities through file access, database connections, API integrations, and other contextual services.

Clients

Checkout awesome-mcp-clients and glama.ai/mcp/clients.

Tutorials

  • Tool Definition Quality Score (TDQS)
  • Model Context Protocol (MCP) Quickstart
  • Setup Claude Desktop App to Use a SQLite Database

Community

  • r/mcp Reddit
  • Discord Server

Legend

  • 🎖️ – official implementation

  • programming language

    • 🐍 – Python codebase
    • 📇 – TypeScript (or JavaScript) codebase
    • 🏎️ – Go codebase
    • 🦀 – Rust codebase
    • #️⃣ - C# Codebase

Note

Confused about Local 🏠 vs Cloud ☁️?

  • Use local when MCP server is talking to a locally installed software, e.g. taking control over Chrome browser.
  • Use cloud when MCP server is talking to remote APIs, e.g. weather API.

aiSummary.oneLiner: A curated directory of production-ready and experimental servers implementing the Model Context Protocol (MCP) for AI integration.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Awesome MCP Servers is a central repository that catalogs server implementations for the Model Context Protocol, an open standard for AI interaction. It organizes servers that extend AI model capabilities by securely connecting them to local filesystems, remote databases, API integrations, and other contextual resources. The list categorizes implementations by language and framework, distinguishing between official SDKs and community experiments. It serves as a discovery platform for developers looking to build context-aware AI applications without reinventing resource connectors.
keyFeatures: Curated categorization: Organizes servers logically by integration type, programming language, and official versus community status.
Broad integration discovery: Catalogs tools for connecting AI models to databases, filesystems, and external APIs seamlessly.
Framework indexing: Lists essential frameworks and SDKs for building custom MCP servers in various programming languages.
Quality scoring: Highlights resources like the Tool Definition Quality Score to encourage robust server implementations.
Community tracking: Provides links to active discussion spaces, tutorials, and quickstart guides for new developers.

useCases.title: AI capability expansion
useCases.description: Developers building custom AI assistants can browse the directory to find pre-built servers for querying local databases or reading specific file formats.

useCases.title: Protocol discovery
useCases.description: Engineers new to the Model Context Protocol can use the repository to find official SDKs and quickstart tutorials.

useCases.title: Server implementation reference
useCases.description: Creators building new MCP servers can examine existing high-quality implementations for architectural inspiration and best practices.

useCases.title: Client integration testing
useCases.description: Teams developing MCP clients can find a diverse array of servers to validate their application's compatibility and robust tool calling.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: This directory is for AI developers, tool builders, and software engineers working with the Model Context Protocol. It requires an understanding of how AI agents interact with external context providers.
